title: Watch (Mark 13)
hook: the Temple will fall, no one knows the hour, so watch
carry: finish today as if it matters

segments.voice: Yesterday, mites: the widow gave more than all the rich, because she gave all she had. Your line was all she had. Today they leave the Temple, and the week ends on one word.

Master, look at these stones! Look at these buildings! Men from Galilee are walking out of the Temple in the big city, and one disciple can't help himself. Jesus looks and says every stone will be thrown down. Then he climbs the Mount of Olives, sits facing the Temple, and four disciples ask him quietly: when? What follows is a long answer, the whole of chapter thirteen.
screen: `LOOK AT THESE STONES!` → `EVERY STONE THROWN DOWN.` → `WHEN? A LONG ANSWER.`

segments.voice: First, the stones. In the Douay-Rheims: "There shall not be left a stone upon a stone, that shall not be thrown down." History records that Roman armies later destroyed the Temple, after a revolt. For Mark's first readers, that may have been recent memory, or still to come. Second, the troubles: wars and rumors of wars, earthquakes, famines, false messiahs, families divided, persecution. Hard to hear. But he keeps saying: don't be alarmed. The end is not yet. Hold on. Third, the surprise: "But of that day or hour no man knoweth, neither the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father." Not the angels. Not even the Son. Christians have wrestled with what it means that the Son doesn't know; the Church reads it in light of his true humanity, and of what was his to reveal. What the verse plainly does is leave no room for a date. Fourth, the doorkeeper. A man goes on a journey and tells the doorkeeper to stay awake, because the master might come back in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning. Some readers notice those four times return in the next chapters: the supper in the evening, the garden at night, Peter at cockcrow, Pilate in the morning. And the speech's last line: "And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch." This week in Mark: the children, the rich man, Bartimaeus, the fig tree, Caesar's coin, the widow. And now, one word for everyone.
screen: `NOT A STONE UPON A STONE.` · `THE END IS NOT YET.` · `NO ONE KNOWS THE DAY OR HOUR.` · `THE DOORKEEPER STAYS AWAKE.` · then, large: `WHAT I SAY TO YOU, I SAY TO ALL: WATCH.`

segments.voice: Watching doesn't mean staring at the sky or reading the news in a panic; it means being awake to what's in front of you. Think through the rest of today and find one unfinished thing you've been putting off, or one person you haven't really paid attention to, and choose to finish it, or face them, before you sleep. If you pray, you can offer the rest of the day.
Watch. The last word of Jesus's speech on the Mount of Olives: stay awake, because no one knows the hour. Today's word.
Your line: finish today as if it matters. Awake, not on autopilot. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics hear Jesus's call to watch at the start of Advent each year, and profess in the Creed that Christ will come again, while the Church teaches that no one can know the day or the hour.

chat.says: Did Jesus tell his friends when the world would end?
options: No. He said no one knows the day or hour, so watch: stay awake.
Yes, he gave a date, but the disciples forgot to write it down.
Yes, he said it would end the day the Temple stones fell.
chat.meaning: Of that day or hour no man knoweth, Jesus says. The speech ends with one word for everyone: watch.

notes: Douay-Rheims Mark 13:2, 13:32 and 13:37 given from memory; confirm.

The Son's not knowing (13:32): the script says only that the Church reads it 'in light of his true humanity, and of what was his to reveal' (cf. CCC 474). A Keeper should confirm this summary is adequate.
Dating of Mark relative to AD 70 is debated; the script says the news 'may have been very recent'. Confirm.
The mapping of the four watches onto the passion (14:17, 14:41?, 14:72, 15:1) is a known reading (e.g. R. H. Lightfoot); presented as 'some readers notice'. Confirm.
